authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses a lossless CST against TWO grammars, chosen by file suffix: KerML and SysML have two start symbols, and sv2_syntax::parse requires a Language with no default (ADR-0014). It reads packages, imports, aliases, FLOW USAGES (SysML 8.2.2.16: both FlowDeclaration alternatives, the `of` payload in all three PayloadFeature forms, and flow ends of one, two or more segments), annotating elements as members, KerML's eight classifiers and its Feature in both forms, SysML's eight definitions plus PortDefinition, seven usages with all five feature specializations, and both keywordless usages. It reads the DECLARATION LAYER of requirements, constraints, calculations and actions: RequirementDefinition, ConstraintDefinition, CalculationDefinition, ActionDefinition and their three specialised bodies (RequirementBody, CalculationBody, ActionBody), SubjectMember, RequirementConstraintMember, ReturnParameterMember, ActionUsage and PerformActionUsage -- and the second alternative of ActionBodyItem, the first of the CONTROL-FLOW LAYER, whole: InitialNodeMember (`first X;`) and the ActionTargetSuccessionMember* after it in its TargetSuccession form (`then X;`, with a SourceEnd and a ConnectorEnd over OwnedReferenceSubsetting), and the THIRD over the behaviour usages it has: SourceSuccessionMember (`then action a;`, and `then part p;` in the two other item productions that admit it) and the `then X;` targets after a BehaviorUsageMember -- and the CONTROL NODES, ControlNode whole (MergeNode, DecisionNode, JoinNode, ForkNode, SysML 8.2.2.17.3) owned through ActionNodeMember, ActionBehaviorMember's second alternative, with the same `then` prefix and target loop, in action and calculation bodies only. The target loop reads ALL THREE of ActionTargetSuccession's alternatives, so the production itself is marked: TargetSuccession, GuardedTargetSuccession (`if <expr> then X;`, SysML 8.2.2.17.8) over GuardExpressionMember, TransitionSuccessionMember, TransitionSuccession and EmptyEndMember -- a TransitionUsage, not a SuccessionAsUsage, told from IfNode and from a ConditionalExpression result by the `then` its guard must reach, and DefaultTargetSuccession (`else X;`), told on its one reserved keyword. ALL FOUR ActionBodyItem ALTERNATIVES ARE NOW READ over the elements this parser has: the fourth is GuardedSuccessionMember over GuardedSuccession (`first a if x then b;`, with the optional `succession` declaration), the only succession that writes its own source and the only alternative that takes no target-succession suffix, over FeatureChainMember@sysml and OwnedFeatureChainMember@sysml (8.2.2.17.5). The SUCCESSION PAIR is read in both languages: SuccessionAsUsage@sysml (8.2.2.13.3, `first a then b;` and `succession s first a then b;`, a NonOccurrenceUsageElement over UsagePrefix) and Succession@kerml with SuccessionDeclaration@kerml (8.2.5.5.3, `succession a then b;` and its FeatureDeclaration form), both over ConnectorEndMember. Its SysML sibling BindingConnectorAsUsage@sysml (8.2.2.13.2, `bind a = b;` and `binding b : T bind a = b;`) is read too, and so is its KerML counterpart, BindingConnector@kerml with BindingConnectorDeclaration@kerml (8.2.5.5.2, `binding a = b;`, `binding ab of a = b;`, and the empty `binding { end feature ... }`). AssertConstraintUsage@sysml (8.2.2.20) is read in both alternatives -- `assert not? constraint <decl> <body>` and `assert not? <reference> <spec>? <body>` -- as a BehaviorUsageElement, so a `then` may precede it and target successions follow it in an action body; ConstraintUsage@sysml, the unasserted `constraint c { }`, is not. The expression layer reads the fifteen precedence tiers, the postfix pair FeatureChainExpression and BracketExpression, and now the INVOCATION -- InvocationExpression over ArgumentList in both its positional and named forms -- and the reference layer reads OwnedFeatureChain. 218 of 554 GRAMMAR UNITS (39.4%), usages owned through the four usage memberships of 8.2.2.6.1 rather than DefinitionMember -- counted in ADR-0015's live units, where a production the two languages state differently is two units, not in the inventory's 558 names. Diagnostics are typed: Parse::errors() returns Diagnostic, each with a TextRange, a namespaced code and a severity, and OffsetMap is the single designated offset boundary. The reference grammar is DERIVED IN FULL and FROZEN at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b: 554 of 554 live units verified in both languages. The RUST parser accepts 71 of 253 .sysml and 18 of 58 .kerml corpus files, recorded per file in tests/corpus-accepted.txt and ratcheted by scripts/corpus_sweep.py: the set may grow and must never shrink.

RESOLVED: positional, and the position cannot be reached from both sides. A '[' reached from UsageDeclaration's FeatureSpecializationPart is a MultiplicityRange (SysML 8.2.2.6.6); a '[' reached after a primary expression operand is a BracketExpression (KerML 8.2.5.8.2). The hypothesis held for every corpus shape. The decisive line is `attribute mass : MassValue[1] = 1200 [kg];`, which writes BOTH roles and parses: multiplicity_part is reachable only from feature_specialization_part, which sits inside UsageDeclaration, and a UsageDeclaration is finished before the ValuePart's '=' is read, so the two can never contend for one token. What separates the productions themselves is the OPERAND: a BracketExpression has one before the '[' and a MultiplicityRange has none, which is what tests/rejection/bracket-expression-needs-an-operand.sysml holds. The corpus also writes a bracketed name (`[one]`, `[spatialCF]`, `[source]`) that is indistinguishable from a multiplicity bound by CONTENT, which is why content was never a candidate rule. Both roles are implemented and 297 corpus files are no longer blocked on this; acceptance went 32 to 39 .sysml when BracketExpression landed.

Is MAX_DEPTH = 400 in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs the right recursion limit, and should it be configurable? It was introduced because the recursive expression parser OVERFLOWED THE STACK, which aborts the process and so is strictly worse than the panic invariant 3 forbids. Measured thresholds before the guard: unary operators between 2000 and 5000 levels, parenthesised expressions and nested bodies between 5000 and 10000. 400 is far past anything a person writes, but it is a number nobody derived from a source, and it changes what the parser accepts.

WIDENED by the postfix expressions. DEPTH IS A PROPERTY OF THE TREE, NOT OF THE PARSER'S RECURSION, and the feature chain proved it: `postfix_tail` is a LOOP and uses no stack at all, yet a 50000-link chain aborted a test thread, because every link wraps the last and the tree is as deep as the chain is long. Folding also stopped being linear at that size. Chains and brackets are therefore counted against the same budget as nested bodies. Anything else that folds -- IndexExpression, FunctionOperationExpression, CollectExpression, SelectExpression, all of which join the same loop -- must count too, and the loop is the place to enforce it once.

Nothing in the gate compares a CITED CLAUSE against what the comment claims of it, and this session produced SIX instances across three review passes -- enough to call it the repository's characteristic defect rather than a run of bad luck. They split into two kinds.

  (2) `calculation_definition` said CalculationDefinition is NOT an OccurrenceDefinition 'unlike the sibling it shares a body with'. It IS one, via ActionDefinition > Behavior, where ConstraintDefinition reaches it via Predicate. The CONCLUSION was right and the ARGUMENT was false, which is the shape nobody rereads.
  (3) and (4) `definition_element` and `usage_element` cited SysML 8.2.2.6.1 for the DefinitionElement/UsageElement alternation; both are stated at 8.2.2.5.2, and 8.2.2.6.1 merely USES DefinitionElement inside DefinitionMember.
